subject: Hardware fence: physical & network isolation evidence for SOC 2 review
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@nimhealth.com>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: Peter Chu <p.chu@nimhealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Hardware fence proof request for SOC 2

Rafael,

As part of our SOC 2 readiness checklist, Nimbus needs concrete evidence of the physical/network "hardware fence" you described during the demo. Specifically we need:
- Port-level ACL + switch config extracts showing tenant-port isolation (serial numbers preferred)
- Photos of rack placement and labeled switch serials for the dedicated/private appliance cluster
- A network diagram that highlights the inline appliances (NVAs) used for egress filtering and the separate HSM/KMS enclave for private deployments
- Any attestation that cryptographic keys for private customers are not co-located with multi-tenant hosted key material

Can you provide these items or an estimated delivery date? If this should go to your security team, please loop them in.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Soto
SecOps Lead, Nimbus Health
From: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@nimhealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-05T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hardware fence proof request for SOC 2

Elena — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Kim (security architecture) and Marcus (site ops) to pull the artifacts.

Quick notes:
- We maintain a physical separation in our Private offering via dedicated racks and management-plane VLANs; Dedicated customers can also be placed behind a per-tenant inline appliance (NVA) that enforces egress controls.
- We will provide switch config extracts that include port ACLs and show VLAN tagging and MAC-level isolation where applicable.
- For the KMS/HSM boundary: Private deployments use a customer-specific KMS instance (customer-managed keying or dedicated HSM cluster) — we'll include the attestation PDF.

Kim/Marcus — can you confirm what we can share (serials, photos) and whether any redaction is required before sending to Nimbus? ETA EOW?

- Rafael
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, Elena Soto <elena.soto@nimhealth.com>, Peter Chu <p.chu@nimhealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T09:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hardware fence proof request for SOC 2

Thanks Rafael — taking point. Deliverables attached and links below. Summary of artifacts included:

1) network-diagram-hardware-fence-v2.png (attached) — annotated diagram showing:
   - Dedicated private racks on separate Top-of-Rack (ToR) switches with isolated management VLANs.
   - Inline NVAs for tenant egress (per-tenant or per-pool depending on customer profile).
   - HSM/KMS enclave physically isolated in a separate rack and on a distinct subnet with ACLs limiting management-plane access.

2) switch-config-extracts.txt (attached) — minimal extracts from switch configs showing:
   - port 1/0/11: tenant-A uplink configured as access vlan 210 (private rack), port ACL applied (deny internet by default, allow egress via NVA)
   - mac-address-table entries and VLAN tagging for ToR aggregation
   - example MACsec enablement on inter-rack links where requested; note: MACsec is selectively enabled for customers requiring link-level encryption (we can enable for Nimbus Private).

3) rack-photo-serials.pdf (attached) — photos of the private cluster rack, front and rear, with serials annotated. We redact staff badges but leave device serials and vendor labels visible.

4) kms-separation-attestation.pdf (attached) — short attestation from infra/security stating that customer keys for Private deployments are provisioned into a customer-dedicated KMS HSM partition and are never exported to the shared control plane.

Notes and caveats:
- We have redacted management VLAN names that contain internal project IDs; serial numbers and port IDs are unredacted.
- For Dedicated (reserved capacity) customers sharing a private pool, physical appliances are rack-isolated per-pool; for fully private (air-gapped) customers we can provide additional photos and on-site witness if required by your auditors.
- I included a Drive folder with full configs: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_hardware-fence-evidence

If you need raw console logs or additional network captures (pcap), we can schedule a secure transfer; otherwise the attached extracts should satisfy the SOC 2 auditor's request.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Staff Security Architect, Redwood Inference
From: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, Elena Soto <elena.soto@nimhealth.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, Peter Chu <p.chu@nimhealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hardware fence proof request for SOC 2

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Kim. A couple follow-ups from Nimbus' vendor checklist they asked we confirm explicitly before they hand to auditors:
- Can you confirm whether MACsec is in production on the ToR-to-aggregation links for Private racks? If not by default, can we provide config snippets showing how to enable it and an estimated time to turn it on for Nimbus?
- Please enumerate the exact switch serial numbers (as shown in the attached PDF) mapped to rack IDs and port IDs used in the extracts so the auditor can correlate.
- Confirm that KMS attestation includes a statement that keys are created inside the HSM and never leave the partition (Kim's attestation looks good but auditors sometimes want specific wording).

Marcus — if you can add the rack-to-serial mapping in the Drive folder (JIRA-SEC-9283) that will close out the serial-number ask.

I'll hold until we have the MACsec confirmation and the mapping; once those are in place I'll forward to Elena and Nimbus' audit contact.

-Rafael
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@nimhealth.com>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, Peter Chu <p.chu@nimhealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-07T15:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hardware fence proof request for SOC 2

Rafael/Kim/Marcus — thanks, this looks thorough and will likely suffice for the initial SOC 2 evidence packet. Two quick asks from our auditor:
- If MACsec is not yet enabled in production, please include the exact config steps and the earliest date you can enable it for Nimbus' racks.
- For the KMS attestation, can you include the sentence: "Customer keys are generated within the HSM partition and private key material is never exported or stored in plaintext outside the HSM."

Once we have those, we will bundle with our auditor and follow up if they request on-site validation. Appreciate the responsiveness.

Best,
Elena
